nervous-system.def: The body’s communication network of neurons, made of the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system.

cns.def: The brain and spinal cord, which take in information, make decisions and send out commands.

spinal-cord.def: The column of nerve tissue inside the backbone that carries messages between the brain and the body; part of the central nervous system.

pns.def: All the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord, linking the central nervous system to the body; made of the somatic and autonomic nervous systems.

somatic.def: The part of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles and carries sensations from the body.

autonomic.def: The part of the peripheral nervous system that controls automatic functions such as heart rate, breathing, digestion and glands; made of the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.

sympathetic.def: The division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for action: it speeds the heart, widens the pupils, slows digestion and increases sweating.

parasympathetic.def: The division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy: it slows the heart and lets digestion resume.

neuron.def: A nerve cell: the basic cell of the nervous system, specialized to receive and send information.
